newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH 1997 WHOLESALES, RETAIL SALES TO RISE -KKL.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH 1997 WHOLESALES, RETAIL SALES TO RISE -KKL.

text.p: The value of wholesales would rise 5.5 percent this year after rising 5.3 percent in 1996 and the retail sales value would rise five percent after rising 4.1 percent excluding cars in 1996, a trade group said on Thursday.

The Finnish Federation of Commerce and Trade (KKL) said in a statement that retail sales of automobiles were forecast to rise 10-15 percent this year and that the forecast five percent rise in the value of its members' 1997 retail sales excluded the impact of car sales.
"The current year will be the best year of the 1990s for the trade sector's sales development," KKL said.

Its survey of members found expectations of continued growth this year as well in sales volumes as in the value of sales. Household purchasing power is expected to increase 3-4 percent this year, the federation said.

In 1996, the value of KKL members' wholesales rose 5.3 percent to 115.50 billion markka and the value of federation members' retail sales (excluding cars) rose 4.1 percent to 117.95 billion markka, it said.

In retailing, the value of automobile sales rose 15 percent, sales of pharmaceuticals and other health care products rose nine percent, department store sales rose seven percent and hardware store sales rose 4.8 percent, KKL said.
